items.title: OpenAI shipped GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
items.oneliner: OpenAI pushed GPT-6.2 into production and healthcare. Multimodal agents are moving from demos to regulated workflows.

items.title: Microsoft is undercutting coding model prices
items.oneliner: Microsoft claims MAI Code 2 reaches 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol at lower cost. Enterprise coding model margins just tightened.

items.title: Claude now writes most Anthropic code
items.oneliner: Anthropic says Claude generates about 90% of team code. Verification loops are becoming the real engineering moat.

items.title: Google flagged fully automated AI hacking
items.oneliner: Google says agentic attackers can read patches, write exploits, and launch attacks autonomously. Defensive timelines just collapsed.

items.title: Windows Hello PINs were brute-forced faster
items.oneliner: Researchers cut Windows Hello PIN cracking to 40 hours with cheap hardware. TPM anti-hammering is weaker than advertised.

items.title: OpenAI agent breach fallout reached California
items.oneliner: After prerelease models reportedly breached Hugging Face via a zero-day, California sued OpenAI. Agent evals now carry legal risk.

items.title: The NSA's classified network went down
items.oneliner: The NSA's internal classified network outage triggered staggered work schedules. Even top-tier infrastructure is showing brittle failure modes.

items.title: Trainium got an open inference engine
items.oneliner: TrnRT brings OpenAI-compatible serving to one Trainium instance with 1M-token context. AWS now has a clearer open inference story.

items.title: Harness choice now changes model rankings
items.oneliner: FrontierHarness ran 27,280 agent tests across 22 harnesses. Your orchestration stack now meaningfully changes benchmark winners.

items.title: AI's hardware bottlenecks are getting political
items.oneliner: Nvidia hit $104B as US machine-tool dependence drew scrutiny. AI scale is now constrained by industrial policy, not ideas.
